notes: This leaf has two large pencil drawings, three small mapping rows, a group-extension diagram, one loop relation, and a footer number 107. No date, title, or separately written author page number is visible.

All parts of both drawings were inspected against C’s TikZ: contours, polar ovals, equator segments, meridian endpoints, dashes, small-circle arc breaks, arrowheads, labels, and local residues. Relative geometry is a manual TikZ approximation of the hand drawing; it is not claimed to reproduce individual graphite grains or every incidental retracing.

The upper sphere’s lower-left meridian points from the lower pole toward the circle at 1. Its circle at 1 has four short arcs with heads at both ends. A second tight crop checked the neighboring circle at i after this recurrent arrow issue was identified: that circle instead has one head per short arc, as C already coded. The broken arcs at −i and −1 have no distinct independent arrowheads in the supplied full-resolution half.

The third small mapping is live z with a leftward arrow from an unwritten right-hand expression. The extra diagonals retrace z; they do not establish a cancellation. Nothing is added to the blank end of the arrow.

The middle group glyph is a smooth cursive capital A with subscript 4. Mathcal A is chosen as the nearest visual typesetting, with the limitation that handwriting does not uniquely determine a modern font family. The abstract alternating-group interpretation was checked separately; it did not decide the appearance of the letter.

The lower north label remains unsure 0 because it consists of several overtraced oval forms. The multiple loops are reproduced, and are not treated as a secure deletion or as a newly discovered authorial question mark.

The central accented beta has a visibly wavy overhead stroke. Both right-hand labels have the same eta formation: left upright, n-like arch, long right descender. No expected path nomenclature was used to replace the written η by H’s γ.

The final right-hand annotation reads η relevé, symétrique de and stops there. H’s trailing illegible placeholder has no corresponding remaining text on the sheet. The missing complement is not supplied.

The lower equator retains faint, partly rubbed-looking strokes above-left of the present −i. They resemble an older −i label and circle fragments, but whether they were erased deliberately, merely retraced, or abandoned without cancellation cannot be settled. They are reproduced lightly with an unsure −i reading, not as a certain struck deletion.

At the lower north pole, the small chord-like arrow rises toward the right, and a second leftward head lies on the back rim. At the lower south pole, the head previously coded by C as a short detached polar arrow is attached to the descending dashed meridian; no duplicate head is added. The front descending meridian also meets the upper/back rim of that oval.

H was supplied only as a prose description of each drawing; no external H drawing file was supplied. This reading does not judge unseen project drawings, does not count prose versus TikZ syntax as a discrepancy, and does not transcribe H’s descriptive introductions or editorial notes as manuscript prose. H rows identify concrete labels, arrow decorations/directions, or placeholders missing or misstated in the available description.

The only mathematical checks actually performed were the elementary four-element Möbius subgroup calculation and a finite permutation computation for the abstract alternating-group extension. The order and base paths of the displayed loop relation were not independently proved from this diagram. No authorial verification claim or authorial doubt sentence is written here.
No OCR, recognition library, external research, or LaTeX compilation was used. The static source file was edited directly, with the page-specific crops retained as the evidence.

check_events.statement: On the complex projective line, s(z)=−z and t(z)=1/z are commuting involutions and generate the four transformations z, −z, 1/z, −1/z.
check_events.place: The two live complete small mapping rows at upper right.
check_events.outcome: Verified algebraically in this run: s²(z)=z, t²(z)=z, and s(t(z))=t(s(z))=−1/z; the four rational maps are distinct. The formulas extend across 0 and ∞ as Möbius transformations. This supports the Klein-four structure but does not complete the unfinished third mapping.

check_events.statement: If the cursive A₄ denotes the alternating group on four letters, its normal Klein-four subgroup is isomorphic to F₂² and its quotient is cyclic of order 3, giving 1→F₂²→A₄→Z/3Z→1.
check_events.place: Group-extension diagram to the right of the upper sphere.
check_events.outcome: An actual Python enumeration of the 24 permutations on four symbols selected the 12 even permutations. V={identity,(01)(23),(02)(13),(03)(12)} had size 4, was closed, every element squared to identity, and every conjugate by an even permutation remained in V. The computed left cosets numbered 3 and their element orders were 1 or 3. Thus the stated abstract extension was verified. This computation was not used to infer fraktur or to alter the handwritten capital’s font.
